previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and morbid obesity was admitted for acute abdominal pain and diagnosed with an incarcerated ventral hernia causing bowel obstruction. She underwent urgent surgical repair with mesh placement and adhesiolysis, then remained intubated in the ICU due to respiratory failure from underlying lung disease and pulmonary edema. She developed ventilator-associated pneumonia, treated successfully with a 10-day course of meropenem. She was extubated on postoperative day 8, advanced to a regular diet, and mobilized with physical therapy. Her heart failure was managed with diuresis, and her anticoagulation was resumed. She was discharged to rehab with a JP drain that was later removed, stable vital signs, and improved respiratory and surgical status.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old female with past medical history of 
chronic respiratory failure secondary to COPD on home O2, 
diastolic CHF, atrial fibrillation, OSA and obesity 
hypoventilation syndrome type 2 diabetes, chronic venous stasis 
wounds, admitted ___ w worsening lower extremity ulcers 
and diastolic CHF, improving with wound care and diuresis, able 
to be discharged to rehab 

# Leg Pain / Venous Ulcers / Venous Insufficiency - Patient 
admitted with bilateral weeping wounds and increasing leg pain; 
exam revealed no signs of purulence or focal super-infection.  
Concern was for worsening of venous stasis ulcers secondary to 
lower extremity edema (combination of heart failure as below and 
poor compliance with leg elevation and wraps).  Patient was seen 
by wound care service and treated with wound care as follows: 
""Cleanse wound with wound cleanser then pat dry apply soothe and 
cool to dry intact tissues cover each leg with 2 large adaptic - 
nonadherent dressing followed by 1 extra large sofsorb wrap with 
kerlix"".  Diuresed as below.  Complicating factors remained 
patient frequently declining to elevate legs or allow them to be 
wrapped.  Continued gabapentin for pain.  She initially was 
ordered for daily dressing changes, but given the complexity, 
incontinence, and soaking of the dressing changes, she required 
changes TID

# Acute diastolic CHF - admitted with worsening lower extremity 
edema and weeping leg wounds as above.  Per reports from 
assisted living, she had previously been frequently noncompliant 
with sodium restricted diet and would often drink large volumes 
of soda.  Given elevated BNP and clinical picture patient was 
started on IV diuresis, with PO liquid restriction and heart 
healthy diet. Patient improved over subsequent 4 days.  
Discharge weight was 131.73 kg   (290.41 lb)

# Atrial fibrillation - Patient also found to have poor rate 
control on admission, which may have been complicating her 
diastolic CHF above.  No signs volume depletion, pain, anxiety, 
infection or embolism.  Discussed with prior outpatient NP who 
reported that prior metoprolol doses have been as high as 100mg 
daily.  Increased dose of metoprolol succinate to 75mg daily 
(from 50mg) and then changed to Metoprolol short acting 50mg TID 
with better control.  Continued rivaroxoban. 

# ___ / Metabolic Acidosis - Secondary to cardiorenal syndrome.  
Cr 1.4 on admission up from baseline 0.8.  Improved to baseline 
over several days with diuresis.   

# Asymptomatic bacteruria - patient found to have positive urine 
culture for Ecoli resistant to multiple antibiotics.  UA had no 
bacteria and patient denied all symptoms. Given her multidrug 
resistance, the risks of treatment far outweighed the benefits 
in a patient who was not demonstrating symptoms of active 
infection.  

# COPD -  continued home fluticasone and Spiriva

# Obstructive Sleep Apnea - has chronically declined CPAP; 
counseled her without change in her behavior. 

# Seizures - continued lamotrigene

# GERD - continued PPI 

# Diabetes type 2 - per report has previously declined insulin 
at assisted living; started sliding scale insulin regimen while 
here, as patient was agreeable to this.  Would consider 
continuing and consider addition of long-acting insulin should 
patient require it. 

Transitional Issues
- Had asymptomatic bacteria during this admission, which was not 
treated; if patient develops symptoms consider treating
